rules.title: Statewide just cause eviction (Tenant Protection Act, Civ. Code § 1946.2)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without a just cause stated in the written termination notice. Just cause is either at-fault (e.g. nonpayment, breach, nuisance) or no-fault (e.g. owner move-in, withdrawal from rental market, government order, demolition or substantial remodel).
rules.key_value: 12 months of occupancy (24 months if adult tenants were added to the lease before 24 months and not all tenants have 12 months)

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential tenancies of 12+ months, except housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years, qualifying owner-occupied or single-family properties with non-corporate owners who gave the required notice, dormitories, transient hotels, certain care facilities, deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing, and properties covered by a local just cause ordinance.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Exempt: a separately alienable single-family residence or mobilehome whose owner is not a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member, if the tenants received the required written exemption notice. Also exempt: owner-occupied residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms, and owner-occupied duplexes.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Does not apply to mobilehome homeowners. Does not apply to housing restricted as affordable or subsidized for very low, low or moderate income households.  Tenancy must be continuous and lawful for 12 months.  Waiver of rights is void.  Owner failure to comply voids the termination notice.  Section is repealed January 1, 2030.  Housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years is exempt unless it is a mobilehome.  Exemptions also cover transient and tourist hotels, nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, adult residential facilities, and school or institutional dormitories.  Single-family owner-occupied residences and mobilehomes are also exempt.  Housing with a shared bathroom or kitchen where the owner lives on the property is exempt.  A two-unit property where the owner occupies one unit at the start of the tenancy and continues to occupy it is exempt, unless a unit is an ADU or JADU.  Properties with qualifying exempt owner status must give written notice of the exemption in the rental agreement for tenancies commenced or renewed on or after July 1, 2020 (July 1, 2022 for mobilehomes).  Residential real property that is alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit is exempt only if the owner is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member (or mobilehome park management) and the notice requirements are met.  Housing deed-restricted as affordable is exempt.  Local ordinances adopted on or before September 1, 2019, and more protective later ordinances, apply instead.  The section is operative April 1, 2024.

rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotels; nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care and licensed residential care facilities; school and higher-education dormitories; shared-facility housing with an owner-occupant; single-family owner-occupied residences (up to two units or bedrooms rented) and mobilehomes; owner-occupied duplexes; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable residential property whose owner is not a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member and who gave the required notice; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; mobilehome homeowners; property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before 9/1/2019 or a more protective later ordinance.
rules.interaction: Does not apply where a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019 applies, or where a later local ordinance is more protective (with a binding local finding). A property cannot be subject to both. Less protective local ordinances adopted after September 1, 2019 are not enforced unless this section is repealed.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

rules.title: Relocation assistance or rent waiver for no-fault terminations
rules.requirement: When an owner terminates a covered tenancy for no-fault just cause, the owner must either pay relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent, and must state this right in the termination notice. Failure to strictly comply voids the notice.
rules.key_value: 1 month of rent (paid within 15 calendar days of service of the notice, or waived for the final month)

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenancies covered by the just cause requirement of § 1946.2 that are terminated for no-fault just cause, regardless of tenant income.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Same owner-based exemptions as the just cause requirement.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies only to no-fault terminations. A tenant found at fault for conditions triggering a government or court vacate order is not entitled to relocation assistance. The assistance is credited against any other relocation assistance required by other law.

rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as the just cause requirement; no relocation assistance where the tenant is at fault for conditions triggering a government or court vacate order.
rules.interaction: Credited against any other relocation assistance required by any other law.
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy.

rules.title: Owner move-in termination conditions and tenant re-offer
rules.requirement: An owner-occupancy no-fault termination is valid only if the intended occupant moves in within 90 days after the tenant vacates and lives there as a primary residence for at least 12 consecutive months. Otherwise the owner must offer the unit back to the former tenant at the same rent and lease terms and reimburse reasonable moving expenses beyond any relocation assistance paid.
rules.key_value: 90 days to move in; 12 consecutive months of occupancy

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenancies covered by § 1946.2 terminated for owner or family member occupancy; for leases entered on or after July 1, 2020 (July 1, 2022 for mobilehomes), requires tenant written agreement or a lease provision allowing it.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Owner must be a natural person with at least a 25% recorded interest, or a qualifying related-owner group, or a natural person owning through an LLC or partnership. Not available if the intended occupant already occupies a unit on the property or a similar vacant unit exists.

rules.quoted_span: Clause (i) applies only if the intended occupant moves into the rental unit within 90 days after the tenant vacates and occupies the rental unit as a primary residence for at least 12 consecutive months.
